subject.title: Feature: Streaming TTS pipeline for voice calls (sentence-level LLM→TTS→audio)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a provider-generic streaming speech contract for classic voice calls, and what first provider/carrier scope must be supported before it becomes a supported feature?
rationale: The central request crosses response generation, plugin speech contracts, telephony playback, cancellation, and provider compatibility; source-level mechanics cannot safely choose the permanent API boundary or support promise.

options.title: Sponsor an additive streaming contract
options.body: Define a plugin-owned async speech-stream capability with explicit buffered fallback and land a bounded first carrier/provider implementation with live latency and barge-in proof.

options.title: Limit scope to current early-TTS improvements
options.body: Keep the existing first-completed-block optimization and document realtime voice as the low-latency alternative without adding sentence-level classic-pipeline streaming.

options.title: Defer pending voice-call roadmap
options.body: Leave the issue open without implementation until an owner commits to the provider and carrier support matrix.

recommendation.title: Sponsor an additive streaming contract
recommendation.body: Define a plugin-owned async speech-stream capability with explicit buffered fallback and land a bounded first carrier/provider implementation with live latency and barge-in proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current issue discussion and feature history place this person closest to the voice-call architecture and provider-scope decision.
